title: Jaunpur Sultanate
capsule: The Jaunpur Sultanate was an independent Muslim polity founded in 1394 by Malik Sarwar, a eunuch lord of the Delhi Sultanate, who established his capital at Jaunpur (in present-day Uttar Pradesh) after the collapse of Delhi authority during Timur's 1398 invasion. The Sharqi sultans became notable patrons of Sufi learning and distinctive Jaunpuri architectural style, blending Afghan and local idioms most visibly in the great mosques built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi (r. 1402–1440). The sultanate was destroyed by the Lodi sultan Bahlul Khan Lodi, who defeated the last Sharqi sultan Hussain Shah at the Battle of Ghaghara (c. 1479) and annexed Jaunpur to the Delhi Sultanate by 1482.
